rationale: OWNER RULING 2026-08-19 (relayed via the portfolio_positioning lane, verbatim intent): 'For the calculators — one submission covering both writers and treat it as a precondition.' This round is the TOOL-writer half of that one logical change, and its rationale names both writers explicitly so no half can ever read as the whole: (1) store_generated_component — the SECTION-level writer — was fixed in round fc3ac5f4 (APPROVED r1, commit 17d883333, PROVEN LIVE on v1.0.1315: both replicas stamp 590ca3a20, ancestry TRUE, COMPONENT_COLLISION_DIVERTED literal present, fake-sha control clean); (2) create_tool_component — THIS round — is the same design fact at TOOL level, RFC_036: content_components.function is unique fleet-wide for library tools (idx_cc_tool_function_unique, measured live: UNIQUE btree(function) WHERE component_level='tool' AND forked_from IS NULL AND is_active) while a tool's identity is per-site, so a site-specific native rebuild of a tool the library also offers dies on SQLSTATE 23505 at save_tool — while the work item reports COMPLETE (RFC_036 §1; the real message only in orchestration_states __step_error). RFC_036 §9.1 proves there is no config-only interim: 'this row is forkable by other sites' and 'this row blocks any rebuild of that tool' are the SAME partial-index predicate, so freeing the index any other way makes the template un-forkable, which the owner's 2026-08-17 direction forbids. THE FIX IS RFC_036 §9.3 AS WRITTEN, owner-directed 2026-08-19 ('framework ownership of all 63 tools, so the 2 blocked tools must be unblocked'): immediately before the INSERT, look up a library tool claiming this function (the index's own predicate) and, if one exists, set the new row's forked_from to its id. It is semantically true, not a dodge — a site-specific native build of a tool the library also offers IS a site copy, which is what forked_from means everywhere else and the shape deploy_tool_to_site already creates (deploy_tool_action.go:294-312). The index keeps guaranteeing what it exists for: one canonical library entry per tool function. Naming does not collide between the two fork producers (RFC_036 §9.2 checked it: deploy forks use library NAME + domainSlug, this generator uses FUNCTION + domainSlug — different strings). Blast radius measured in RFC_036 §9.3: fires only when a library entry already claims the function — 4 of the webdesign lane's 63 tools today; every other generation is byte-identical (pinned by test: no claim → forked_from NULL, the pre-change write). A lookup READ error fails OPEN to today's behaviour — no fork, and a real collision is refused LOUDLY by the unique index, never guessed (pinned by test). Deliberately DIFFERENT from the section-level remedy, on measured grounds recorded in RFC_036 §11 per the architecture seat's tracking ask on fc3ac5f4: at tool level the fork ESCAPES the partial index and this action links the page itself, so fork-invisibility to selectors is irrelevant; at section level every selection path filters forked_from IS NULL, so the diverted row had to stay base. Consumers: tool-generator workflow (save_tool — its 2 parked builds start succeeding), deploy_tool_to_site (unchanged; its fork lookup keys on library NAME so it cannot mistake a generated fork for its own — see risks for the double-copy tail), the webdesign_tool_rebuilds lane (unblocks tool-ab-test-calculator and tool-meme-generator, the last 2 of 63), the ~140-domain portfolio buildout (the add_tool route will fire on those sites; this closes the same wall there), RFC_034 conversion programme (converts by id; forks are already in its census). No new action input keys — no RFC_022 budget movement. What this pair is a PRECONDITION for, per the ruling: portfolio wave 1 (~50 sites) does not start until both writers are landed.
submitter: bugfix_311_component_keys (session bugs_open/311, 2026-08-19; tool-writer half per the owner's one-submission ruling)

plan.summary: create_tool_component gains the RFC_036 §9.3 library-claim check: before the INSERT, look up a library tool claiming the function (component_level='tool' AND forked_from IS NULL AND is_active — the idx_cc_tool_function_unique predicate exactly); if found, the new row is born with forked_from = the library row's id, exempting it from the index by construction while keeping the index's guarantee intact. No claim → byte-identical to today. Lookup error → fail-open to today's loud index refusal. Mutation-proven sqlmock tests pin all three arms.

edits.rationale: The lookup predicate is the index's own predicate, verbatim, so 'a library entry claims this function' and 'the INSERT would violate idx_cc_tool_function_unique' cannot drift apart. Fail direction on a read error is towards today's behaviour: no fork, and the unique index refuses a real collision loudly — never a silent guess.
edits.sketch:
// --- Library claim check (RFC_036 §9.3) ---
    var libraryToolFork interface{} // nil unless a library entry claims the function
    {
        var libID string
        lookupErr := params.DB.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
            SELECT id::text FROM content_components
            WHERE function = $1
              AND component_level = 'tool'
              AND forked_from IS NULL
              AND is_active = true
            LIMIT 1
        `, function).Scan(&libID)
        switch {
        case lookupErr == nil && libID != "":
            libraryToolFork = libID
            logger.Info("CreateToolComponentAction: library tool claims this function — new component forks from it (RFC_036 §9.3)", ...)
        case lookupErr != nil && lookupErr != sql.ErrNoRows:
            logger.Warn("CreateToolComponentAction: library-claim lookup failed — proceeding without fork; a real collision will be refused loudly by idx_cc_tool_function_unique", ...)
        }
    }

    _, err = params.DB.ExecContext(ctx, `
        INSERT INTO content_components (
            id, name, display_name, function, component_level,
            category, description, html_template,
            is_active, is_dark_section, created_from,
            source_agent_type, source_orchestration_id, forked_from
        ) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'tool', $5, $6, $7, true, false, 'generated', $8, $9, $10::uuid)
    `, componentID, componentName, displayName, function,
        category, description, htmlContent,
        nullIfEmpty(params.ExecutionContext.Sender.AgentType),
        nullIfEmpty(params.ExecutionContext.OrchestrationID),
        libraryToolFork)

edits.rationale: Three arms, each pinning the INSERT's forked_from argument via WithArgs so the tests are mutation-proof: deleting the fork wiring flips the argument and the match fails — RUN this session: mutation applied, test failed on 'argument 9 expected [library id] does not match actual [nil]', restored, suite green. The walk deliberately ends at the INSERT (it returns an error) — everything after is the adopt tests' pinned territory and the argument assertion has already fired.

The new lookup statement lands between two statements the existing adopt tests pin in ordered sqlmock walks; without this they would 'pass' by silently exercising the new Warn/fail-open branch (sqlmock's unexpected-query error is swallowed by the fail-open). Pinning the lookup in the shared preamble keeps those tests exact.

func expectPreamble(mock sqlmock.Sqlmock) {
    mock.ExpectQuery("SELECT domain FROM sites")...
    mock.ExpectQuery("FROM content_components cc")...
    mock.ExpectQuery(`forked_from IS NULL`).
        WillReturnError(sql.ErrNoRows) // RFC_036 §9.3 lookup: no claim
    mock.ExpectExec("INSERT INTO content_components")...
    mock.ExpectQuery("url_shape")...
}

grounded_in: OWNER RULING 2026-08-19 (relayed via portfolio_positioning): 'For the calculators — one submission covering both writers and treat it as a precondition.' Recorded in RFC_036 §9.5 (restated) and bugfix_311_component_keys/NOTES.

RFC_036 §9.1: 'That predicate is the index predicate. idx_cc_tool_function_unique fires on component_level='tool' AND forked_from IS NULL AND is_active — so "this row is forkable by other sites" and "this row blocks any rebuild of that tool" are the same condition.'

RFC_036 §9.3: 'look up a library tool claiming this function (component_level='tool' AND forked_from IS NULL AND is_active, no site filter). If one exists, set the new component's forked_from to its id. Nothing else changes. … It is semantically true, not a dodge. … Blast radius is small and enumerable: it only fires when a library entry already claims the function — 4 of this site's 63 tools today.'

RFC_036 §9.2 (the naming non-collision, checked): 'the fork builds name = <library component NAME> + '-' + domainSlug … while the generator builds name = <FUNCTION> + '-' + domainSlug. Different strings, so content_components_name_key does not stand in the way.'
Measured live 2026-08-19 (\d content_components): 'idx_cc_tool_function_unique' UNIQUE, btree (function) WHERE component_level = 'tool'::text AND forked_from IS NULL AND is_active = true.

RFC_036 §1 (the failure shape this closes): 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_cc_tool_function_unique" (SQLSTATE 23505) … The work item nevertheless reported complete with error NULL; the real message was in orchestration_states.collected_data->'__step_error'. Nothing was built.'

Section half's state, so this round cannot be read as the whole either: fc3ac5f4 APPROVED r1 covers store_generated_component only; LIVE on v1.0.1315 (stamp 590ca3a20 both replicas, merge-base ancestry TRUE, COMPONENT_COLLISION_DIVERTED literal present, fake-sha negative control clean); ZERO real exercises yet (no-demand zero) — the loanzy lane's next clean-domain build is the agreed real-world test with incumbent md5 baselines pinned.

Cross-lane trap stated so no reader over-claims: §9.3's lookup predicate sees only LIBRARY TOOL rows — a section-level incumbent claims nothing in it (correct for the index), so this edit fixes RFC_036's wall and does NOT touch bugs_open/311's section-level deadlock, which fc3ac5f4's live fix owns.
plan.risks: 1) The double-copy tail: a site that first gets a GENERATED fork (this path, name = function+slug) and later runs deploy_tool_to_site for the same library tool would not be recognised by deploy's existing-fork lookup (it keys on library NAME + slug — different string), so a second site copy could be created; the collision then surfaces LOUDLY at the page layer (pages_site_id_name_key / the adopt path), not silently. Reviewers should confirm loud-at-page is acceptable for this tail, or ask for a follow-up that widens deploy's fork lookup. 2) Semantics of forked_from: the generated template's BYTES are not derived from the library parent — forked_from here asserts 'site copy of this tool', RFC_036 §9.3's stated meaning, matching the owner's 2026-08-17 fork direction; anything that reads forked_from as byte-lineage (e.g. diff-against-parent tooling) would mislead on these rows. 3) Fail-open lookup: on a transient DB error the fork is skipped and a real collision dies on the index exactly as today — behaviour never degrades below status quo, but a retry after a transient error succeeds where the first attempt failed, which can look like flakiness; the Warn line names it. 4) Forked rows are exempt from idx_cc_tool_function_unique by construction — two generated forks of the same function for the SAME site are prevented by the name UNIQUE constraint (same name string), racing inserts fail loudly. 5) The already-exists probe (JOIN page_components) still precedes this: a site whose fork is already linked to a page returns early, unchanged.
